q: a benchmark of 100 web application specifications (50 private validation, 50 held-out test) with 964 browser-based workflows comprising 10,131 substeps
r: Include: new benchmark for end-to-end web application development by LLMs from specifications, with cost, latency and evaluator-alignment analysis.

q: This workin-progress paper introduces a token-level cost model grounded in the documented mechanics of a production agent
r: EC6: modelled per-commit cost on two SWE-bench repositories (issue-repair style tasks, nothing run), so excluded as issue repair.

q: This paper presents a systematic audit of technical debt in AI-generated software
r: Include: compares code quality and maintainability (code smells) of agent-generated multi-file projects, evaluation-method and project-level.

q: Each task is run both ways, five times each, inside the real agent.
r: Include: cost-aware, correctness-gated evaluation harness with repetitions and baseline for coding-agent efficiency tools; contribution is the evaluation method.

q: Across 300 artifacts generated by three coding agents, 68.3% execute successfully out-of-the-box
r: Include: controlled comparison of three coding agents building software artifacts from requirement prompts, with a new execution-reliability measure.

q: BDD-Bench evaluates coding agents against executable behavioral specifications across chronological repository changes.
r: Include: new benchmark where agents implement features from executable Gherkin specifications over an evolving codebase, 13 models, 3 runs each.

q: The code is then converted into an executable file, creating a tangible project.
r: Include: new project-level benchmark (ProjectEvalPlus) evaluating agents building whole projects with end-to-end acceptance tests.

q: agent-mode configurations improve average performance from 28.2% to 45.0%, but do not eliminate the architectural failures.
r: Include: published ASE 2026 version of the Needle in the Repo benchmark (kept over the arXiv preprint 800486182); new maintainability metric for agent repository edits.

q: This paper presents an example of the design process of a singleshot vibe-coded LSC tool for a given lifelog data layer.
r: IC1: single-shot prompt-design case study producing one lifelog search tool, not an evaluation or comparison of coding agents.

q: We have presented a comprehensive review of AI agentic programming.
r: Include: systematic survey (with search method) of coding agents, taxonomy, evaluation and benchmarking; secondary studies are kept.
